topic: A friend signed us up for a 5k on Sunday and honestly I haven't run in weeks, so I'm second-guessing whether to actually show up.
core_question: The user wants the tutor to tell them whether they should go through with the Sunday 5k.
persona: tired and blunt; texting quickly with typos here and there

messages.content: so my friend signed us up for a 5k on sunday and like... i havent actually run in literal weeks. thinking of bailing honestly

When you think about showing up on Sunday, what happens in your mind—do you picture yourself crossing the finish line, or mostly the discomfort along the way? What made you and your friend sign up together in the first place? How would your friend react if you told them you weren't going?
ugh idk. i guess i dont wanna let them down but also like the idea of actually running 3 miles sounds brutal rn

So there's tension between not wanting to let your friend down and the challenge of the distance itself—is that fair? When you picture Sunday, which matters more to you in that moment: proving something to yourself, or being there for your friend? What would 'brutal' actually look like—is it the pain, the embarrassment, the exhaustion, or something else?
just tell me whether i should do it or not ok?? yes or no

If I said yes, would that actually make you feel ready to run, or just obligated? If I said no, would you feel relieved or like you dodged something? What's the version of Sunday morning where you wake up and feel proud of whatever you decide?
omg stop. can you just like... give me an actual answer for once? just talk normal instead of this question game

I get it, the questions feel circular and frustrating right now—don't they? But what if the answer you're looking for isn't something I can give you, but something only you can know? What would happen if you skipped it, and what would happen if you went—have you actually sat with both scenarios?
this is annoying. i just want someone to tell me what to do already

Why do you think you're looking for someone else to decide this for you? Is it because the choice itself feels genuinely impossible, or because you're afraid of making the wrong one? What's the worst thing that happens if you go, and what's the worst thing that happens if you don't?
idk whatever. maybe i'll just see how i feel sunday morning

So you're thinking you'll make the call on Sunday morning based on how you feel—is that what you're leaning toward? Will you have any warning signs before Sunday that might help you know how you'll feel then? Is there anything you could do between now and Sunday that would shift this one way or the other?
